subject: Private IaC toolchain triage & SOC2 evidence handoff (Acme HealthSystems)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jules Martin <jules.m@acme-health.com>, devops@acme-health.com, security@acme-health.com
Date: 2027-01-23T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private IaC toolchain triage & SOC2 evidence handoff (Acme HealthSystems)

Hi team,

Acme's security team just asked for a compact evidence package to support their SOC2 review of the private deployment. They want proof of the following items specific to the private/VPC deployment we built for them:

- Terraform state locking + remote backend config (cross-account role for state writes)
- Idempotent Ansible roles used for node bootstrap (audit logs showing runs)
- Helm overlay strategy for customer value patches (how secrets are injected)
- Network layout: private subnets, egress controls, interface to on-prem via Direct Connect
- CI gating: pipelines that prevent merges without module tag/signing and smoke-test results

I attached an initial evidence bundle (iac-evidence-bundle_v1.tar.gz) that pulls logs and snippets from the branch we used. Also attached: network-diagram.pdf and a short helm-overlay-proposal.md that documents the overlay pattern we used.

Request: please triage the bundle and reply with: 1) any missing pieces they will ask for in audit (especially around KMS usage / envelope keys), 2) a minimal additional artifact we can hand them within 48 hours, and 3) whether the GitLab pipeline link below is sufficient as an audit trail, or we should capture artifacts elsewhere.

GitLab pipeline: https://gitlab.redwood.ai/acme/priv-iac/pipelines/12345
Evidence drive folder: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1aBcD-evidence

If possible, let's lock in a 30-min triage call tomorrow at 09:00 PT to align before I respond to Jules.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Programs Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs:
- iac-evidence-bundle_v1.tar.gz (tar.gz, ~4.1MB)
- network-diagram.pdf (PDF, 820KB)
- helm-overlay-proposal.md (MD, 14KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jules Martin <jules.m@acme-health.com>
Date: 2027-01-23T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private IaC toolchain triage & SOC2 evidence handoff (Acme HealthSystems)

Naomi — quick pass from infra: thanks for pulling this together. A few inline notes and an attached module diff (module-diff.patch) with proposed doc comments.

> - Terraform state locking + remote backend config (cross-account role for state writes)
- We use an S3 backend with DynamoDB locking and a cross-account assume-role. The evidence bundle includes the backend.tf snippet but not the assume-role policy. I'll add the policy and the CloudTrail query that shows AssumeRole events in the last 90 days.

> - Helm overlay strategy for customer value patches (how secrets are injected)
- Concern: the current helm-overlay-proposal.md shows secrets being templated into a values overlay. For SOC2 we should show a KMS-wrapped secrets flow or point to sealed-secrets/helm-secrets patterns and the KMS key policy. I propose we capture a small demo run that uses KMS envelope encryption and put the rendered secret (redacted) in the evidence bundle.

> - CI gating: pipelines that prevent merges without module tag/signing and smoke-test results
- The pipeline link is fine but it will be stronger if we also include signature verification artifacts: GPG signatures for tagged modules and the pipeline job logs for the last three successful smoke tests. I can export logs from job 12341-12343.

Operational asks:
- I will add: assume-role policy, CloudTrail AssumeRole logs, pipeline job logs, and a tiny README explaining where to find the KMS key id in AWS (no secrets in the repo).
- Note: we should avoid uploading full private key material. Keep KMS IDs and redacted ARNs.

I'll push a follow-up bundle in ~3 hours (module-diff.patch attached).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs:
- module-diff.patch (text patch, 9KB)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jules Martin <jules.m@acme-health.com>
Date: 2027-01-23T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private IaC toolchain triage & SOC2 evidence handoff (Acme HealthSystems)

On 2027-01-23 10:12 Naomi Feldman wrote:
> Acme's security team just asked for a compact evidence package to support their SOC2 review of the private deployment.

Thanks Naomi — two network-specific items to flag that might come up in the audit:

1) Egress controls: the network-diagram.pdf shows a NAT Gateway pattern in public subnets to handle third-party updates. For SOC2 they may ask about outbound filtering — we should include the managed NACLs and the AWS Network Firewall rule group id we used. I can export the firewall rule JSON and add it to the evidence bundle.

2) VPC endpoints and DNS: the deployment uses interface endpoints for SSM/Secrets Manager and a private hosted zone for service discovery. Include the Route53 hosted zone id and the VPC association list (redacted). The hosted zone id is sufficient; do not include IPs.

Action: I'll gather the firewall rule JSON and the Route53/VPC association artifacts and drop them in the drive folder by end of day. Also recommend we create a simple runbook snippet showing how we rotate the NAT/egress rules if Acme requests changes.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Network Security Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Jules Martin <jules.m@acme-health.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-23T18:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private IaC toolchain triage & SOC2 evidence handoff (Acme HealthSystems)

Hi Naomi / team — thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifications from Acme security:

- KMS integration: we only need the KMS key id and the key policy excerpt showing the cross-account principal. We do not need key material.
- Audit trail: the pipeline links are OK but we need attestations for who approved the merge (GitLab approver emails) for the three tagged module releases.
- Timing: if you can provide the expanded bundle and the runbook snippet within 48 hours, Acme can accept that for the audit intake.

Also, can you include one example of an Ansible run that demonstrates idempotency — either logs or a short playbook run output? That will help our auditors.

I'll be available tomorrow morning PT at 09:00 for the triage call.

—Jules Martin
Security Engineering Manager, Acme HealthSystems
jules.m@acme-health.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jules Martin <jules.m@acme-health.com>
Date: 2027-01-24T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private IaC toolchain triage & SOC2 evidence handoff (Acme HealthSystems)

Thanks all — great notes. Quick summary and owners before the call at 09:00 PT: 

- Karthik: add assume-role policy, CloudTrail AssumeRole query, pipeline job logs (jobs 12341-12343), and GPG signature verification artifacts. Drop into drive folder.
- Priya: export firewall rule JSON and Route53/VPC association metadata (redacted) and add runbook snippet for egress change.
- Marissa: capture one Ansible run output demonstrating idempotency (redacted timestamps/hostnames) and a short README describing the role test harness.
- Naomi: package a sanitized evidence bundle (iac-evidence-bundle_v2.tar.gz) with readme, push to the drive folder and share link with Jules when complete.

Next steps: we will iterate on v2 in the triage call and aim to hand off v3 (final) to Acme by EOD tomorrow if no blockers.

Meeting: 2027-01-24 09:00 PT — join via the usual Redwood conference bridge (link in calendar).

Naomi
